tagline.text: A shopping complex in downtown Cagayan de Oro, open since 1991

location.label: Location
location.text: Limketkai Drive, Lapasan, Cagayan de Oro City

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (a good indoor option when it is hot or rainy)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,500 (estimated for meals and transport, excluding shopping)

children.text: Limketkai Center is a mixed-use shopping complex in Cagayan de Oro's central business district, open since 1991. The two-level mall holds more than 350 stores, with Robinsons and Shopwise as anchors, and a skywalk links it to a hotel, making it a handy base for a day in the city.

Limketkai Center is a large mixed-use shopping complex in the heart of Cagayan de Oro (CDO), in the Lapasan district of the central business district. According to the official website, it opened in 1991 and celebrated its 35th anniversary in 2026; it is developed and operated by Limketkai and Sons. Wikipedia describes the whole development as a complex of about
40 hectares

, with a mall floor area of roughly 100,000 square meters. It started as a mostly single-storey, open-air shopping strip, but after Robinsons Cagayan de Oro opened in 2002 and the center was converted into a two-level, fully air-conditioned mall in 2003, it began to look much as it does today.

The official store directory lists more than 350 stores inside the mall. Robinsons Department Store, Robinsons Supermarket and the Shopwise hypermarket serve as the main anchors, while clothing, shoes, electronics, mobile phones, general goods, bookstores and optical shops are spread across the floors. On the second floor, the Lolika Food Hall gathers stalls such as Bigby's, Jollibee and Burnout Grill Lechon Haus, and familiar chains such as McDonald's, Starbucks, KFC, Shakey's and Mang Inasal are plentiful, so even travelers who are not yet used to Filipino food can easily get a meal.

It is not only a place to shop. Banks and ATMs, money changers, pharmacies, medical and dental clinics and courier branches are all here, and government offices such as the Department of Tourism (DOT), Bureau of Immigration, LTO and PSA also have branches in the complex, so it is a familiar stop for Korean residents who come downtown for visa extensions or paperwork. Within the complex are the Limketkai Luxe Hotel and a pod-style accommodation for travelers, and a skywalk connects the hotel and the mall. It is a good place to rest for a day on the way to nearby destinations such as Dahilayan, Tinago Falls and Camiguin, using Cagayan de Oro as your base.
Keep in mind that this is a place to experience city life and conveniences, not a destination for natural scenery or ruins. Plan about
2–3 hours

to look around the mall itself, or half a day if you include meals and a cafe stop. All of the cinemas permanently closed on March 1, 2025, so if you are hoping to catch a movie, look for another mall.

blocks.title: Lolika Food Hall and the chain restaurants

children.text: The second-floor Lolika Food Hall is the mall's main dining area. Everything from popular Filipino fast food to grilled dishes and lechon stalls is gathered here, so families can easily choose what to eat. Avoiding the lunch rush around noon makes it easier to find a seat.

blocks.title: Grocery shopping at Robinsons and Shopwise

children.text: At Robinsons Supermarket and the Shopwise hypermarket you can pick up souvenir foods such as snacks, coffee and dried mango, along with household goods, all in one go. It is also handy for stocking up on water, snacks and toiletries if you stay at a downtown hotel or an Airbnb.

This outdoor strip of restaurants and bars inside the complex comes alive in the evening as the open-air tables fill up. It suits anyone who wants a cold beer or a meal late in the evening. Check each venue for its opening hours late at night.

blocks.title: The Atrium and the Rotunda event venues

children.text: According to Wikipedia, the Atrium is an event venue that seats about 4,500 people and hosts conventions and concerts, and events are also held in the circular Rotunda. You can find out what is on during your visit on the weekly events page of the official website.

The official website lists Pickle World on the second floor, with pickleball, badminton, a climbing wall and roller skating, as well as karting, karaoke and children's play areas. They are useful when you need something to do with kids on a rainy day.

blocks.title: The skywalk and Limketkai Luxe Hotel

children.text: The skywalk runs toward the Robinsons mall and the Luxe Hotel, so you can get around without crossing the road. The complex also has facilities such as the hotel's rooftop pool and restaurants, so you can plan a stay that keeps lodging in the same place.

Major banks such as BDO and BPI, ATMs, money changers, pharmacies (Mercury Drug and Watsons), couriers (2GO and LBC), and clinics and dental offices are all gathered here. It is convenient for withdrawing cash, buying medicine and sending parcels in one trip.

blocks.title: From an old strip to a modern complex

children.text: The way the center grew from an open-air strip in 1991 into an air-conditioned mall in 2003, and then into a complex with a hotel, offices and residential towers, is a chapter in the development of downtown Cagayan de Oro. Many recent reviews say that renovations have improved its appearance and cleanliness, though some areas still feel dated.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: The mall and the arcade, from lunch to evening

children.text: Arrive when the mall opens at
. Take care of errands such as currency exchange, ATMs and buying a SIM card first, while it is quiet.
Browse souvenir foods and household goods at Robinsons Supermarket or Shopwise. It is easier to buy heavy items later.
Have lunch at the second-floor Lolika Food Hall. It gets crowded around noon, so going a little earlier or later makes it easier to find a seat.
Take your time browsing the clothing, shoes and electronics floors, and rest at a cafe if you need to.
As the sun goes down, head to Rosario Arcade for dinner and drinks.
Wrap up before the mall closes at
and head back to your hotel. It is safer to take a taxi or Grab at night.
Movies are left out of the plan because all of the cinemas closed in March 2025.
Go in when the mall opens and enjoy a leisurely brunch at the second-floor food hall.
With children, use indoor facilities such as the kids' play area or Pickle World. Check prices and reservations on site.
Keep walking along the skywalk toward Robinsons and the hotel to stay out of the rain.
When the rain stops, have dinner at Rosario Arcade.
There are direct flights from Manila (NAIA) to Laguindingan Airport (CGY), the gateway to Cagayan de Oro. The flight takes about
1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours
, and airlines and schedules change often, so check before booking.
Flights from other cities, such as Cebu, are also available. Check airline announcements for routes.

items.title: From Laguindingan Airport to the city

children.text: The trip from the airport to the city takes about
1 hour
. A fixed-fare airport shuttle (Magnum Express) is listed at about ₱200–250, and Limketkai Center is given as one of its drop-off points. Fares can change, so confirm before boarding.
Taxis and Grab are quoted at about ₱600–1,200, and guides differ widely. Some taxis do not use the meter, so agree on the fare before you get in.
Some guides also mention a bus fare of around ₱100–150, but this may not be a regular route directly from the airport, so check locally.
The official website says the mall has 13 entrances and 3 taxi stands. There is also a jeepney zone.
From downtown hotels you can go by taxi or Grab. For jeepney routes and fares, it is best to ask locally.
If you stay at the Limketkai Luxe Hotel or elsewhere in the complex, you can walk.
Limketkai Center is indoors, so you can visit at any time of year. It works especially well as a backup stop during the hottest part of the day and in rainy weather.

Mornings right after opening and afternoons before dinner tend to be quieter, while weekends, holidays and the Christmas season are crowded. Opening hours can change on holidays, so check the latest announcement.

The official website says the complex includes the Limketkai Luxe Hotel, a pod-style accommodation for travelers (Travelers Pod), and The Loop Tower, a condo-style tower that offers short stays. Connected to the mall by a skywalk, they are easy to move between even late at night. Check prices and make reservations directly on each property's website.

You can easily eat at the chains inside the mall, and Rosario Arcade offers open-air dining and drinks. The hotel and complex also list restaurants serving local Cagayan dishes (such as Kagay-anon Restaurant) and a steakhouse. As for Korean food, the official website lists a samgyeopsal place and a shabu-shabu restaurant in the mall, so confirm they are still there before you visit.
The mall is open daily from
to
, though hours may differ on holidays. Some restaurants and convenience stores stay open later.
With as many as 13 entrances, set meeting points by the exact entrance or store name. There are also 3 taxi stands, so check which one you are heading to.
It is a good place to handle currency exchange, ATMs, a SIM card and the pharmacy in one trip. Rates differ between money changers, so compare two or three.
The air conditioning is strong, so bring a light jacket.
Limketkai Center is given as a drop-off point for the airport shuttle, so if your first night's hotel is nearby, the shuttle is convenient.
Even in a mall, keep your belongings close in a crowded food hall or event venue.
If you are hoping for a cinema, remember that all of them closed in March 2025.
Checking the weekly events page on the official website before your visit helps you avoid missing events at the Atrium and the Rotunda.
In July 2013 there was a bombing at Rosario Arcade in this complex. It now operates as an ordinary commercial facility, but check local safety announcements before you visit.
There may be security procedures such as bag checks when entering the mall, so allow extra time.
Some airport taxis do not use the meter, so agree on a fare before getting in or use Grab.
Avoid walking alone late at night around the arcade and nearby streets, and take a taxi or Grab home.
Opening hours and store operations may change on holidays and during events, so check the latest announcement.
Tenants change often, so if you are heading for a particular shop, confirm through the official directory or by phone (088-856-5228).
